findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the disposer
findings.body: After callers invoke the returned disposer, the handler remains registered and continues processing future messages. Repeated attach/dispose cycles retain handlers and cause duplicate processing and listener growth.

findings.title: [P2] Clear the polling interval during cleanup
findings.body: Calling the returned cleanup function no longer stops polling. The callback continues running after teardown, repeated starts accumulate timers, and the live interval can prevent a Node.js process from exiting.

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned disposer
findings.body:
Any caller that invokes the returned cleanup function still remains subscribed. Subsequent `"message"` events invoke a supposedly detached handler, causing stale-state updates, duplicate handling after reattachment, and listener retention.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Clear the polling interval when stopping
findings.body:
After any caller invokes the returned stop function, `refresh` continues running every second. This can mutate disposed state, accumulate duplicate polling loops after restarts, and keep Node.js processes alive indefinitely.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore message listener cleanup
findings.body:
When callers invoke the returned disposer, the handler remains registered and processes all future `"message"` events. Repeated attach/dispose cycles accumulate duplicate listeners and can leak memory or process messages after teardown.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore polling interval cleanup
findings.body:
Calling the returned disposer no longer stops polling. `refresh` continues running every second after teardown, and in Node.js the retained interval can also keep the process alive indefinitely.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the disposer
findings.body:
Calling the returned cleanup function no longer removes the `"message"` handler. Repeated attach/cleanup cycles retain handlers and their captured state, causing duplicate processing, linear listener growth, and eventual EventEmitter listener warnings.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Clear the polling interval during cleanup
findings.body:
Every `startPolling` call now creates an interval that cannot be stopped. After callers invoke the returned cleanup function, callbacks continue indefinitely, retained closures and timer work accumulate, and in Node.js the live interval can prevent process termination.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
